title: Merlot
description: Plum, softness and the clay of the Right Bank: the world's second most planted red grape.
L: Merlot gives medium to full-bodied reds with plum, black cherry, blackberry and, with oak, chocolate and vanilla. Tannins are softer than Cabernet Sauvignon's, acidity medium. It's approachable young and can age well when grown on great sites. It's the second most planted red grape in the world.

Merlot comes from Bordeaux, first recorded in 1784. Its name may come from merle, the French for blackbird, which loves its ripe grapes. DNA shows its parents are Cabernet Franc and Magdeleine Noire des Charentes, so it's a half-sibling of Cabernet Sauvignon. Its large, thinner-skinned berries explain its softer tannins.
Where may Merlot's name come from?
Merle means blackbird, a bird that loves its ripe grapes.

Look for medium to deep ruby colour, plum and black cherry aromas, and a rounder, softer palate than Cabernet, with less obvious blackcurrant. Cool-climate Merlot can show herbal or green notes; warm-climate Merlot is ripe and fruity, sometimes jammy.
Merlot has larger berries and thinner skins than Cabernet Sauvignon.
Yes. That's why its tannins are softer and its wines rounder.
Merlot gives plum, black cherry and soft tannins
It comes from Bordeaux; its name may mean blackbird
It's a half-sibling of Cabernet Sauvignon
Explain why it suits clay and cool soils

Merlot is the most planted grape in Bordeaux, about 60% of red plantings. It's important in Italy, especially Tuscany and Friuli, and in Switzerland's Ticino. In the New World it grows in California, Washington, Chile, Australia, South Africa and New Zealand's Hawke's Bay.

Merlot buds and ripens one to two weeks before Cabernet Sauvignon. On cool, water-retentive clay soils, where Cabernet would struggle to ripen, Merlot thrives. But early budding exposes it to spring frost, and its thinner skins make it prone to rot in wet weather, and to coulure, poor fruit set.
Match each region to its Merlot role.
Merlot is grown widely, often in Bordeaux-style blends.
When a Bordeaux label says Bordeaux or Bordeaux Supérieur, without a famous commune, it's often Merlot-dominated and made to drink early.
What are Merlot's vulnerabilities in the vineyard?
Merlot ripens easily; in heat it can overripen, not fail to ripen.
Merlot is Bordeaux's most planted grape, grown worldwide
It ripens early and loves cool clay soils
Frost, rot and coulure are its weaknesses

Pomerol is small, about 800 hectares, with no official classification. Its plateau has gravel over clay; the centre has a unique blue clay, rich in smectite, that swells when wet and holds water. Merlot thrives there. Pétrus, almost pure Merlot, grows on this clay. Le Pin and Lafleur are other famous names.

Saint-Émilion, a UNESCO World Heritage town, has about 5,500 hectares. Its limestone plateau and slopes, the côtes, give elegant, long-lived wines; sandier soils below give softer ones. Merlot leads, with Cabernet Franc often important, as at Cheval Blanc and Ausone.
Limestone plateau, Merlot and Cabernet Franc
Which famous Pomerol wine is almost pure Merlot?
Pétrus grows Merlot on Pomerol's blue clay.

Saint-Émilion has its own classification, revised about every ten years: Premier Grand Cru Classé A, Premier Grand Cru Classé B and Grand Cru Classé. It's controversial and was challenged in court. Cheval Blanc, Ausone and Angélus withdrew from it before the 2022 edition. Pomerol has no classification at all.
Pomerol has an official classification like the Médoc's.
Not true. Pomerol has no official classification; reputation alone ranks its wines.
Pomerol's blue clay gives Merlot like Pétrus
Saint-Émilion's limestone gives elegant Merlot and Cabernet Franc
Saint-Émilion's classification is revised; Pomerol has none

In the 1990s, Merlot became the fashionable red in the US: soft, fruity and easy to pronounce. Plantings grew fast, often in hot, high-yield sites, giving bland, simple wines. Quality became uneven, and the name grew associated with mass-market wine.

In the 2004 film Sideways, the main character declares he won't drink Merlot. US Merlot sales growth slowed, while Pinot Noir sales rose. Ironically, his treasured bottle is a 1961 Cheval Blanc, a Saint-Émilion with a large share of Merlot alongside Cabernet Franc.
What wine does the main character of Sideways treasure?
The irony is that Cheval Blanc contains a large share of Merlot.

Merlot makes some of the world's most expensive wines: Pétrus, Le Pin, Masseto in Tuscany. Washington State, Hawke's Bay and parts of Chile make excellent, fresh Merlot. Quality depends on site, yield and picking time, like any grape. The backlash was about overproduction, not the grape.
Sancerre is Sauvignon Blanc from the Loire.
Merlot boomed in the 1990s, often overproduced
Great Merlot, from Pétrus to Masseto, endures

Merlot's soft tannins make it flexible: roast chicken, pork, duck, mushroom dishes, lasagne and medium-rich beef. It handles some umami better than very tannic reds. Lighter styles can even go with salmon or tuna. Avoid very spicy food, which clashes with alcohol.

Serve at 15 to 18 degrees. Simple Merlot is best within three years. Top Pomerol and Saint-Émilion age 20 to 40 years, gaining truffle, leather and earth. Merlot's softer tannins often make it approachable earlier than Cabernet-based wines of the same quality.
Why is Merlot flexible with food?
Soft tannins clash less with a wide range of dishes.
An older Pomerol with a mushroom risotto or truffle pasta is a classic match. The earthy, truffle notes of mature Merlot echo the dish.
Top Pomerol can age for 20 to ____ years.
Great Pomerol develops truffle and earth over decades.
Merlot pairs widely, from chicken to mushrooms
Top Right Bank wines age for decades
Why does Merlot suit Pomerol's clay?
It ripens early and likes cool, water-retentive soils
Clay stays cool; early-ripening Merlot still ripens there.
Match each wine or place to Merlot.
Merlot makes famous wines in several countries.
Merlot ripens later than Cabernet Sauvignon.
Not true. It ripens one to two weeks earlier.
Lime belongs to white wines like Riesling.
Merlot's name may come from merle, meaning ____.
Merlot is plummy, soft and approachable
It's Bordeaux's most planted grape, king of the Right Bank
Its 1990s boom and Sideways hurt its image, not its potential
It's flexible at the table and the best age for decades
